name: libuvc
desc: Cross-platform library for USB video devices
why: A USB Video Class library lets you talk directly to webcams and microscopes, a real door into how USB devices expose streams.

brief.what_it_is: libuvc is a cross-platform C library for USB video devices, built on top of libusb. It talks to any device that exposes the standard USB Video Class (UVC) interface, giving fine-grained control over it. Developers can use it to write drivers for devices that aren't supported yet, or to access UVC devices in a generic way. The README describes USB video devices in general terms and does not mention webcams or microscopes by name.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames it as a way to write drivers for previously unsupported UVC devices, or to reach any UVC device generically without a vendor-specific driver.
brief.how_it_works: libuvc sits on libusb and speaks the USB Video Class protocol to the device, so it can control the device and receive its streams. The README describes two stream-tuning knobs: LIBUVC_PACKETS_PER_TRANSFER_MAX sets the maximum number of isochronous packets in one USB transfer, and LIBUVC_NUM_TRANSFER_BUFS sets how many transfers are queued at once. The README does not explain the internals beyond this.

brief.install_notes: Prerequisites are libusb and CMake. Build from source with git clone, cmake, make, and sudo make install. Optional example and test programs need the BUILD_EXAMPLE and BUILD_TEST CMake flags, and uvc_test needs OpenCV. CMake cache options can be edited in CMakeCache.txt or through a CMake GUI. The README doesn't mention a Homebrew formula, so the brew install path isn't covered there. No accounts, hardware, or runtime setup are mentioned.
brief.standout: It gives direct, generic access to any USB Video Class device through a small C library, with no vendor-specific driver needed. The README also exposes buffer-tuning knobs that matter on constrained platforms.
brief.status: unknown. The README gives no release date, version number, or recent-activity note, and I did not check the repository's commit history or release page.
brief.caveats: The homepage https://libuvc.github.io/ returned no content when fetched, so the docs it points to could not be read. The README says the test program uvc_test needs OpenCV. Streaming can fail with errno=12 on Android, and the README suggests lowering LIBUVC_PACKETS_PER_TRANSFER_MAX as a workaround. The default number of queued transfers is 20 on macOS and 100 elsewhere. The README does not mention microscopes, which the scout note brings up. The licence was not stated in the text I read.
quotes: libuvc is a cross-platform library for USB video devices, built atop libusb.

It enables fine-grained control over USB video devices exporting the standard USB Video Class (UVC) interface, enabling developers to write drivers for previously unsupported devices, or just access UVC devices in a generic fashion.
The documentation for libuvc can currently be found at https://libuvc.github.io/.
